messages:
Sam (Support): opening thread — Acme reports a short burst of 429s in eu-west-1 around 2026-04-02. they provided a few request ids and a small client timeline. sharing for repro & quota correlation.

Priya (Oncall): please paste one full failing request + the response headers (no auth token). need X-Request-Id and client timestamp to map to our logs.

Sam (Support): their failing sample (redacted):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: acme-eu-20260402-07' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-8b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"brief summary"}]}'
```

Response body (trim):

{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error"}}

Response headers they recorded:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 11:22:19 GMT
X-Request-Id: acme-eu-20260402-07
X-RateLimit-Limit: 200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 37
Retry-After: 15

Diego (SRE): good. ask them for a 200 sample from the same client around the spike for header comparison and the client-side timestamps (ms) for +/- 5 requests. also request the client IPs.

Sam (Support): they sent a mini timeline and three IDs: acme-eu-20260402-05, acme-eu-20260402-07, acme-eu-20260402-09. timeline (client local times):
- 11:21:58.734 acme-eu-20260402-05 POST -> 200
- 11:22:05.101 acme-eu-20260402-07 POST -> 429
- 11:22:36.553 acme-eu-20260402-09 POST -> 200

Maya (Eng): please ask them to export a HAR (if browser) or curl --trace-ascii / mitmproxy dump if server-side. if not possible, ask for a curl replay that keeps X-Request-Id unchanged so we can reproduce. also ask for payload sizes and token parameters (max_tokens, temperature).

Sam (Support): they uploaded a sanitized HAR to our intake at https://uploads.redwood.ai/s/ghi789 (internal only). they also attached a short Node replay that reproduced the 429 for them and said the spike was confined to a single VPC NAT IP.

Priya (Oncall): @Diego can you check per-customer quota accounting and per-IP aggregation for the 11:21:50-11:23:00 window in eu-west-1? also verify if any rate-limiter config changed or deploys happened near 11:20 UTC.

Deploy-bot: [notice] rate-limiter config updated 2026-04-02T10:50:00Z -> patch applied

Diego (SRE): noted. I'll correlate X-Request-Id -> internal trace id and pull edge + backend quota counters. if the NAT collapsed many clients we may hit per-IP buckets. will also check for autoscale/limiter counters mismatches.

Maya (Eng): if SRE sees edge headers showing Remaining=0 but backend still had capacity, that suggests a miscount at the edge. check prefix-cache logs for that keyspace as well.

Sam (Support): customer also included a local curl replay sample id acme_replay_010 that produced 429 for them:

```bash
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: acme_replay_010' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-8b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'
```

Diego (SRE): perfect. I'll request the internal trace logs and token accounting for acme-eu-20260402-05..09 and acme_replay_010. if we confirm a limiter edge miscount we'll escalate.

Maya (Eng): request client to avoid rotating keys mid-replay and to keep X-Request-Id stable. also ask them to include the exact Node script they used and the inter-request spacing.

Sam (Support): confirmed with customer — they will not rotate creds and will provide the Node script + optional tcpdump if needed. they asked for an ETA; I gave 24-48h for initial findings.

Priya (Oncall): next steps: Support — gather HAR, Node replay, client timestamps (+/-5). SRE — map req ids, check per-IP aggregation and quota windows. Eng — compare edge X-RateLimit headers vs backend counters and cache behavior.

Diego (SRE): starting log correlation now for acme-eu-20260402-05..09 and acme_replay_010. will post updates here.

Sam (Support): thanks team. I'll attach the HAR link & Node file to the ticket and keep Acme updated. :thumbsup:
